Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment is a chemical cross-linking (CXMS) study using the DSSO cleavable crosslinker to map the interaction between RAC1 and IMPDH2. While the PRIDE metadata says 'No PTMs are included', the methods explicitly describe DSSO cross-linking and the use of XlinkX for identifying cross-linked peptides (CLPs), which requires specific search parameters for the cross-link mass shift and site-level output.

scope: In vitro, a DSSO cross-link reaction was performed with the purified recombinant proteins of GST-IMPDH2 and 6xHis-RAC1 following the manufacturer’s instruction.
The recombinant proteins were purified from IPTG-induced bacterial culture by standard protocols for glutathione-agarose (for GST-tagged IMPDH2 proteins) and Ni-NTA beads (for 6xHis-RAC1).

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The mass spectrometry analysis was specifically performed on purified recombinant proteins (GST-IMPDH2 and 6xHis-RAC1) subjected to chemical cross-linking, not on cell lysates or fractions.

Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: The mass spectrometry proteomics component of this study is specifically a chemical cross-linking (CXMS) experiment using recombinant proteins (GST-IMPDH2 and 6xHis-RAC1) to map interaction interfaces. While the broader paper describes extensive cell-based genetic perturbations (shRNA, mutants), the MS data provided in the PRIDE context is limited to the in vitro cross-linking of these specific recombinant proteins.

Ontology_ProcessingAndDifferential_promp.notes: This is a targeted chemical cross-linking (CXMS) experiment using the cleavable crosslinker DSSO. The primary goal was to identify interaction sites between RAC1 and IMPDH2. Standard bottom-up pipelines will fail to identify the cross-linked peptides without the specific XlinkX-style search logic and MS3 fragmentation handling.
